name: Arizona
summary_text: The July 2026 national legal-risk map places Arizona in its 'Low-Risk' tier: largely refrained from targeting trans adults without taking extraordinary protective steps — it has enacted policies affecting youth but, per the map's author, appears unlikely to extend them to adults. Tucson cancelled its 2026 Pride citing the political and financial climate. Appears on 2026 enacted-lists (flagged: client-side tracker). Around the national score 0.36.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026
sources.claim_summary: Erin Reed's anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update, via Stonewall News): grades every US state's legislative risk for transgender adults; Idaho entered the top 'Do Not Travel' tier (felony bathroom ban, up to 5 years; the map's fourth such state) and South Carolina rose to 'Worst Laws Passed'; catalogues the nationwide federal rollback (passport and legal-document barriers, funding withdrawals, Pride-crosswalk erasure) and several countries' travel advisories for trans travellers. Places Arizona among 'Low-Risk States (AZ, DE, ME, MI, NV, PA, VA, WI, DC)' and notes Arizona and Virginia have enacted anti-trans policies affecting youth but appear unlikely to extend such policies to adults.

sources.title: Where Pride won’t be happening this year
sources.claim_summary: Prism Reports (June 2026): Pride organisers in several cities — including Tampa (FL), Arlington (TX) and Tucson (AZ) — cancelled historic 2026 Pride celebrations, citing a political and financial environment that made supporting queer events nearly impossible and attending them potentially dangerous; in Florida a new law empowers the governor to remove elected officials who support Pride organisations.
